Description

The Activity Flow map updated with what the Process Description blocks now say, with the authors' drawing kept. Receptors stand in the order of the Process Description, left to right. The mast cell holds the eicosanoid network exactly as in the Process Description, with its processes. New in the nociceptor: IL-1β through p38, IL-6 with its soluble receptor on gp130, PKCδ and TRPV1, PGD2 on DP1, CCL2 through Gβγ on NaV1.8, the eicosanoids on TRPV1 and TRPA1, NaV1.7, and ASK1 and MKK3 between TRAF2 and p38. NGF acts on TrkA (NTRK1). Substance P activates the mast cell through MRGPRX2, and the CGRP receptor on the mast cell is removed. The mast cell also has IgE and FcεRI leading to degranulation and histamine, and osteopontin from bone, cartilage, synovium and the mast cell itself acting on integrin αv. New in the spinal cord: the loss of inhibition (KCC2, GABA-A and glycine receptors), PGD2 from microglia on DP1 and DP2, the microglia (ATP, P2X4, p38, BDNF) and the astrocyte (lipoxin A4, FPR2). CGRP and β2 act through Gs, PKA on the action potential and against the glycine receptor, and the AMPA receptors are GluA1 and GluA3. The opioids are agonists, peptides and analgesics, and antagonists, as in the Process Description.

Colour

Red raises pain, blue relieves it, and olive acts both ways or neither. Each glyph takes the colour its name has in the same cell of the assembled Process Description, olive where it has both. The eicosanoid network keeps its own colours. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.
